patterns.pattern: Festival weeks increase category demand by approximately 40% versus a normal week
Competitors typically respond to a price cut within 12 hours during active sale periods, but within 3-5 days otherwise
Price elasticity for this category averages -1.2, meaning a 1% price cut drives roughly 1.2% volume increase
patterns.sample_size: estimated from 18 months of price/volume data

patterns.pattern: Bundling increases unit volume by approximately 25% compared to an equivalent standalone discount
Premium-tier SKUs show much lower elasticity (-0.4) than mid-tier SKUs (-1.5); price cuts move less volume for premium items
Overstock situations that are not addressed within 30 days tend to require deeper eventual discounts to clear
New product launches see 60-70% higher volume response to promotional pricing than mature products
Post-festival demand typically drops 15-20% below pre-festival baseline for about 2 weeks
Stores within the same city cluster show correlated demand; a stockout signal at one store often precedes one at nearby stores within 5-7 days
Holding price when a new low-price competitor enters tends to outperform matching, if the incumbent has a service or reliability advantage
